name: apply 3 — follow-up: form invitation by verdict, one reminder, then Slack escalation

nodes.name: Follow-up schedule
nodes.notes: All timers are derived from stage + timestamps on the sweep cadence, never from Wait nodes, so a restart cannot drop a pending reminder. Shortening REMINDER_AFTER_MINUTES / ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES does nothing unless SWEEP_CRON shortens with them.

nodes.name: Reminder due
nodes.notes: Exactly one reminder: form_reminded_at empty AND the invite older than REMINDER_AFTER_MINUTES.

nodes.name: Escalation due
nodes.notes: Already reminded and silent for another ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES → a human decides. The stage becomes escalated, which is non-terminal: the row resumes its normal path if the applicant acts.

nodes.name: Render form invitation
nodes.notes: The verdict picks the template: fits gets step2-invite, wrong_host gets advised-wrong-host, not_open_source gets advised-not-open-source, unclear gets advised-unclear. DRY_RUN is checked here, at the send site. Templates embedded verbatim from automation/emails/*.md.

nodes.name: Render reminder
nodes.notes: DRY_RUN is checked here, at the send site. Template embedded verbatim from automation/emails/reminder.md.

nodes.notes: apply 2 calls this when it has written verdicts, so an application reaches the invitation in the same pass rather than waiting for the next sweep. It enters at the invitation branch only. The reminder and the escalation stay on the sweep alone, because running them more often is what would duplicate a reminder email.

nodes.name: Claimable for the invitation?

conditions.leftValue: ={{ !$json.form_invite_skipped_at && (!$json.applied_at || DateTime.fromJSDate(new Date($json.applied_at)) < $now.minus({ minutes: Number($env.INVITE_AFTER_MINUTES || 5) })) && (!$json.form_invite_claimed_at || DateTime.fromJSDate(new Date($json.form_invite_claimed_at)) < $now.minus({ minutes: Number($env.STALE_CLAIM_MINUTES || 30) })) }}

nodes.notes: A row another run is already working is skipped. A claim older than STALE_CLAIM_MINUTES (30 when unset) is treated as abandoned, so a run that died cannot strand an application forever. A row whose invitation was skipped because Open Collective had already decided is never claimed again. A row younger than INVITE_AFTER_MINUTES (5 when unset) waits for a later sweep, so a decision made straight after applying, such as a pre-agreed move from another host, lands before the invitation would.

nodes.name: Claim the row for the invitation
nodes.notes: A compare-and-swap, not a hopeful write. The second condition is the value this run just read, null included, so only one of several runs can match. A conditional update that matches nothing returns an empty result and emits no items, which silently skips the row. Everything expensive, the email above all, sits downstream of this node.

nodes.name: Fetch application status before inviting
nodes.notes: The same public account fields the decision sweep in apply 1a and 1b reads. A decision can land on Open Collective before the invitation goes out, for example a move from another host agreed in advance and approved within a minute, and an applicant who has already been decided on must not be asked to fill in the form.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'query($s:String){account(slug:$s){slug ... on AccountWithHost{isApproved approvedAt host{slug} } } }', variables: { s: $json.slug } }) }}

nodes.name: Fetch admin legal names
nodes.notes: One request per row: our own host's legal name, then each admin in oc_admins looked up on its own. Open Collective shows a host admin the legal name of an applying collective's admins only through a top-level account query, never through the collective's member list, and only to a token with the account scope. The host's own profile has a legal name, so an empty one there means the token lacks that scope. No retry: with continueRegularOutput the node turns each failed request into an item rather than throwing, and a failed check only sends the invitation without the request. The response holds legal names, so they stay in this execution's saved data until n8n prunes it. Find admins without a legal name passes on public names only. A ten second timeout keeps a hanging Open Collective from holding the invitation back.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (() => { let admins = []; try { admins = JSON.parse($json.oc_admins || '[]'); } catch (e) { admins = []; } const slugs = (Array.isArray(admins) ? admins : []).map((a) => a && a.slug).filter((s) => typeof s === 'string' && s !== ''); const variables = { h: $json.host_slug }; const declared = ['$h:String']; const fields = ['host: account(slug:$h){ legalName }']; slugs.forEach((s, i) => { variables['a' + i] = s; declared.push('$a' + i + ':String'); fields.push('a' + i + ': account(slug:$a' + i + '){ slug legalName }'); }); return JSON.stringify({ query: 'query(' + declared.join(',') + '){ ' + fields.join(' ') + ' }', variables: variables }); })() }}
